Population increased in Ipswich

The estimated population of Ipswich in 2024 was 140,274 usual residents, a rise of 0.6% since 2023.

This meant that Ipswich's rate of population change placed it about average among local authority districts in England and Wales.

In the period from mid-2021 to mid-2024, the population estimate of Ipswich increased by 0.5%.

Over this slightly longer period, Ipswich was also among the 20% slowest growing local authority districts in England and Wales.

Age profile of Ipswich

The average (median) age stayed at 38.8 years between 2023 and 2024.

You can see how the age profile of Ipswich has changed since 2011 in the population pyramid below.

sections.content:
Ipswich is an area that is classed as urban in nature according to the 2021 Census Rural Urban Classification.

By age category, Ipswich's population of 140,274 usual residents was made up of:

  • 28,471 people aged 0 to 15 years, (20.3%)
  • 87,821 people aged 16 to 64 years, (62.6%)
  • 23,982 people aged 65 years and over, (17.1%)

    • Compared with England and Wales as a whole, Ipswich has a slightly higher proportion of people aged 0 to 15 years (20.3% compared with 18.3% for England and Wales).

Contributors to population change

We look at different flows of people into and out of areas and births and deaths to see what is driving population change in each area.

In Ipswich, the largest contribution to population change in the year to mid-2024 was from net international migration.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Ipswich
sections.subtitle: How the population changed, by component

sections.content:
We estimate that, for Ipswich, between 2023 and 2024:

  • More births than deaths increased the population of 272 people (0.2%). In total, there were 1,501 births and 1,229 deaths in Ipswich.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other areas in the UK) led to a fall in the population of 809 (-0.6%). There were 7,654 people entering the area and 8,463 people leaving the area.
  • Net international migration led to an increase in Ipswich's population of 1,287 (0.9%) as a result of 2,303 people entering the area and 1,016 people leaving the area.
  • Other change (which includes changes to armed forces personnel and prisoners) for Ipswich was less than 0.1%.

Revisions to 2023 population estimates

We regularly revise our initial population estimates as we get more data and methods improve.

Our revised estimate for the population of Ipswich in mid-2023 is 139,497.

Within this, international migration was revised upwards by 834 people and internal migration estimates were revised downwards by 715 people.

Overall, there was an revision upwards of 119 people.
